payload.root_cause: In src/text.js line 11, slugify replaces separator runs with `.replace(/[\s-]+/, '-')` but the regex lacks the global flag `g`. String.prototype.replace with a non-global regex substitutes only the first match, so only the first whitespace/dash run becomes a dash; all subsequent gaps are left as-is (e.g. 'Hello Big  World!' -> 'hello-big  world' because the '! ' is stripped to a space, the first ' ' becomes '-', and the remaining '  ' between 'big' and 'world' is never replaced). Adding the `g` flag (/[\s-]+/g) makes every run collapse to a single dash. Note the adjacent cleanup regex on line 12 (/^-+|-+$/g) already has the flag, which confirms this is an omission, not an intentional design. The fix has no security impact: slugify is a pure string transformation with no eval, interpolation into commands, file, or network access; adding a regex flag cannot introduce injection or unchecked-input behaviour.

payload.rationale: The root cause is the missing `g` flag on the separator-collapse regex in slugify (src/text.js line 11). With a non-global regex, String.prototype.replace substitutes only the first `[\s-]+` run, so every later gap between words is left as raw whitespace/dashes. Adding the `g` flag makes every run of whitespace and dashes collapse to a single '-', which makes both failing assertions pass: 'Hello Big  World!' -> 'hello-big-world' and '  Already-slugged  title ' -> 'already-slugged-title' (the leading/trailing dashes produced by edge runs are still trimmed by the final `/^-+|-+$/g` cleanup). This matches the intent shown by the adjacent regexes on lines 10 and 12, which already use `g`. Security review: this is a one-character change to a pure string transformation — no eval, no dynamic regex construction from user input (the pattern is a static literal, so no ReDoS or injection vector is introduced; the regex is linear-time on the character class), and no new file or network access. The change actually tightens output (all whitespace is removed from slugs), reducing risk if slugs are used in URLs or filenames.
